newsitem.title: ARGENTINA: Argentina gets approval for U.S. beef sales-Menem.
newsitem.headline: Argentina gets approval for U.S. beef sales-Menem.

text.p: The United States has finally approved a 20,000-tonne import quota of Argentine beef and will take its first delivery in April, Argentina's president Carlos Menem said Friday.
"As of April, 20,000 tonnes of fresh Argentine beef is going to begin to be marketed in the United States," Menem said, quoted by state-run news agency Telam.

His comments appeared to signal the end of a long wait for final sanitary approval from the United States for the import quota, which was first announced after big progress in eliminating foot-and-mouth disease in Argentina.
Argentina complained publicly several times in 1996 about what they saw as slow progress in approving the imports.
Argentine beef was for decades excluded from major markets because of foot-and-mouth, but its huge herd of 50 million head has now gone almost three years without an outbreak.
Argentine beef producers hope U.S. approval will help prise open major markets in Asia. Argentina has accused South Korea and Japan of using sanitary rules as an excuse to keep its beef out.
The government hopes beef exports will reach one million tonnes by 2000, although many in the industry think this overly optimistic.
